content.text: : form of chronic otitis media in which
grows from the TM or the auditory canal into the middle ear mucosa or mastoid
: acquired (MC) ⇢ ET dysfun, recurr/chronic otitis media
▪︎= keratinized collection of desquamated epithelial tissue in the middle ear or mastoid
▪︎1° acquired: TM inversion 2/2 chronic eustachian tube dysfun (eg chronic allergies, chronic sinusitis)
▪︎2° acquired: TM perforation or iatrogenic (eg tympanoplasty); granulation tissue → gradual ossicle erosion
▪︎acquired: hx of chronic ear infect or tympanostomy tubes; congenital: no prior hx of chronic ear infect
retraction pocket w/ squamous epithelium & debris (granulation tissue) that often appears as a brown, irreg mass
▪︎cholesteatoma most external to the TM; some 2° cholesteatomas = white mass internal to a healed TM
: ossicle destruction, facial n. paralysis, temporal bone erosion
▪︎conductive HL most commonly ← erosion of the distal portion of the incus
▪︎permanent hearing loss, CN palsy, vertigo, + infect = possible comp
▪︎CT only if extracranial comps suspected (esp w/ systemic illness or signs of localized infect)
excision via mastoidectomy to control d/c &
reconstruction of middle ear structures & sound-
▪︎excision w/ tympanoplasty; mastoidectomy if lesion extends superiorly or posteriorly; ossicular chain recon if significant HL
